title: Ordinary root sessions on enrolled hosts must message each other exactly like local sessions (termal_send_to_session across Windows and macOS)
outcome: After a host is added, an ordinary termal_send_to_session between non-special root sessions on Windows and macOS works in both directions with the same behaviour as a local send, through the existing session/federation core only, with no manual binding, special sender or extra opt-in
acceptance: An ordinary termal_send_to_session from a non-special Windows root session to a non-special macOS root session, and the return send from that macOS session back to the Windows session, each addressed with an explicit host_id plus session_id, are each observed live with: a durable send, the message visible on the remote host, an automatic wake of the recipient, a turn start, a read and ACK by the recipient, and its return message. No specially bound proof sender, manual mailbox or domain binding, or additional opt-in or security step is used.

The ordinary-send contract follows Greg's rule: a bare session_id is deliberately local-only and always sends to the local session; a remote session is addressed only by explicitly giving both host_id and session_id (the existing composite identity, in w-8837's qualified reference form), which routes to exactly that session. A bare id that names no local root gets a refusal whose guidance explains how to address a remote session. One shared routing/delivery implementation in the existing session/federation owner serves local and federated destinations (no new identity scheme, registry, parallel session manager, adapter, sender or wake loop), no send path remains that works only through a manual binding, and unqualified, unverified, revoked or stale-link peers are refused with an explicit error.

Focused tests cover: a qualified local-to-remote and remote-to-local ordinary send; a bare id sending locally even when a session with the same id exists on the other host; the refusal guidance for a bare id with no local root; refusal for an unqualified or stale peer; and the unchanged local-to-local path. The live proof includes the bare-id-stays-local control. A review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher; the change lands through Merger2 and is installed on both hosts.
